key_insight: Deep learning predicted HPV/p16 status from routine vulvar cancer slides more accurately than it distinguished all three molecular subtypes.
clinical_relevance: Slide-based predictions could support retrospective HPV-stratified outcome research when ancillary testing is unavailable, without consuming additional tissue.
method: Extracted features from hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images using H-optimus-1.
Trained attention-based models: HERA for HPV/p16 status and HERMES for three molecular subtypes.
Developed models on 644 patients and tested them on 286 patients from independent cohorts.
evidence_signal: Independent testing yielded an AUC of 0.84 (95% CI 0.75–0.91) for HERA and a macro-average AUC of 0.70 (0.66–0.75) for HERMES; predicted groups also showed prognostic separation.
watch_item: External validation of discrimination and calibration across scanners and populations is needed, particularly given HERA’s 0.68 sensitivity and HERMES’s limited separation of HPV-independent subtypes.
paper_title: Predicting HPV/p16 Status and Molecular Subtypes from Histopathology Slides using Deep Learning in Vulvar Squamous Cell Carcinoma
